why_not_repeat_historical_underbombardme.historical: The short 19-Feb bombardment left many positions intact and the 106th RCT bogged down.
why_not_repeat_historical_underbombardme.branch: GALVANIC/FLINTLOCK learning plus the already-delayed Catchpole clock makes Hill/Watson less willing to trade hours of schedule for an underprepared landing.
why_not_repeat_historical_underbombardme.result: preparatory fire begins earlier and lasts roughly 2-3 hours with planned pauses for carrier strikes; still not a Parry-scale saturation bombardment.

Japanese_defense.branch_strength: better mortar registration, ammo dispersion, local communications and tank dispatchability

landing.terrain: eight-foot-class beach bluff/sand rise still blocks LVT movement and creates congestion; this physical geometry is not solved by better US doctrine
landing.US_progress: initial beachhead secure but inland movement slows under MG/mortar fire

22Feb_afternoon.result: repulsed by Army infantry, Marine reserve, M4s, mortars/artillery and naval call-fire; causes real local disruption but no beachhead collapse

22_23Feb_night.result: penetrates one local perimeter/command-support area in small packets but is contained; no operational breakthrough
22_23Feb_night.US_night_advantage: illumination, shipboard/shore communications and pre-registered artillery improve response; radar is warning/coordination support, not foxhole detection

23Feb_dusk.result: C2 fragmentation leaves only 20-60-man infiltrator groups and isolated positions

armor_exchange.note: reliability makes the three Japanese tanks tactically present for longer, not survivable after loss of the island

organized_resistance_end.night_window: crosses sunset at center; only fragmented infiltration after ~20:00, no new large counterattack

Parry_effect: The 22d Marines reembark/reorganize during 22-23 Feb and Parry saturation fires begin while Eniwetok mop-up is still ending; Parry assault remains feasible on 25 Feb.
